audit_findings.title: Financed reinvestment may escape the owner-earnings deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed 2025 financed asset additions were $780m ($578m software and other intangibles plus $202m hardware), finance-lease principal payments were $345m, and uncommenced finance-lease commitments were $393m
audit_findings.mechanism: Financed maintenance assets can bypass the cash-capex deduction while their depreciation is added back, inflating anchor OE and every forecast year; related interest is already retained in equity-level OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Finance lease payments exclude $ 393 million of legally binding minimum lease payments for leases signed but not yet commenced.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates substantial financed investment, but it does not establish which assets replace consumed productive capacity, which depreciation was added back, or whether principal payments were otherwise captured. The $780m scale equals 17.4% of the $4,490.8m anchor and would reduce the base buy-below value by about $14.10 per share if treated as a recurring dollar-for-dollar OE deduction, so the issue could materially affect value. The actual required deduction remains unresolved rather than demonstrated.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each eligible 2025 D&A add-back to the $1,763m cash capex, $780m financed additions and $345m finance-lease principal payments; identify maintenance versus growth assets, then rerun all scenarios using the resulting normalized maintenance deduction without double counting interest.

audit_findings.title: Recurring merchant funding needs may be absent from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed 2025 net advances were $636m, equal to 14.2% of the $4,490.8m anchor, while the first six months of 2026 produced a computed $112m net merchant-advance inflow and $188m settlement-advance inflow
audit_findings.mechanism: Any recurring increase in merchant and settlement-anticipation receivables is an operating funding requirement classified outside operating cash flow and may require an OE working-capital deduction; matched borrowing and retained interest expense affect the adjustment.
audit_findings.evidence: Net merchant and settlement anticipation cash advances were $636 million during 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The $636m 2025 use would reduce the base buy-below value by about $11.49 per share if it were a recurring OE deduction, which is potentially significant. However, the 2026 reversals show that a single year's net advance flow is not a demonstrated sustainable requirement, and the record does not show how the anchor treats advances, associated income or matched financing. Materiality therefore cannot be established from the normalized amount presently available.
audit_findings.action: Build a multi-year roll-forward of merchant and settlement-anticipation advances, related revenue, credit losses and dedicated borrowings; determine the normalized equity-funded balance growth and rerun OE after deducting only that amount without double counting retained interest expense.

audit_findings.title: The stakes bridge may not be net of guaranteed affiliate debt
audit_findings.magnitude: $471m aggregate guarantee at 2026-06-30 ($482m at 2025-12-31), versus $1,133m stakes_net; recorded guarantee liabilities were $11m at 2026-06-30
audit_findings.mechanism: A guarantee loss would reduce the stakes bridge or create a separate equity claim; default could also impair the included Lending Joint Ventures investment.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has provided aggregate guarantees of $ 482 million associated with the debt of the Lending Joint Ventures and is entitled to receive a defined fee in exchange for its guarantee of this indebtedness.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether stakes_net already reflects the exposure is unresolved, but even a stress loss equal to the entire latest $471m gross guarantee would reduce value by only about $0.87 per share and the buy-below threshold by about $0.61, from $83.42 to approximately $82.81, still well above the $53 market price. The gross guarantee is therefore too small by itself to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the components of stakes_net and whether the recorded $11m liability is already netted; document a bridge stress for full guarantee payment, recoveries and loss of the $90m Lending Joint Ventures investment, but no valuation-input change is required for the present conclusion.

audit_findings.title: Cash added to equity value may not be distributable cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $382m unavailable out of $627m total cash at 2026-06-30; $245m was disclosed as available
audit_findings.mechanism: Only parent-accessible excess cash belongs in the equity bridge; unavailable settlement, regulatory, in-transit and joint-venture cash must be excluded.
audit_findings.evidence: Represents cash associated with: intermediary settlement balances; wholly owned entities subject to regulatory requirements; cash in transit; or cash in our joint ventures that is not available to fund operations outside of the respective entities unless approved by the board of directors of the relevant entity.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge error if the full $627m was added: the latest filing identifies only $245m as available. Removing $382m lowers value by about $0.70 per share and the buy-below threshold by about $0.49, to approximately $82.93 versus the $53 price. The correction is concrete but cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Replace the $627m cash bridge input with the filed $245m available amount, unless a legal-entity schedule demonstrates additional distributable cash, and recompute the bridge and per-share outputs.

audit_findings.title: A disposal gain may remain in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: filed gains were $89m on the contract distribution, $51m on an equity-method investment sale and $82m on sales or remeasurement of other equity investments; computed no-tax upper bound including the full $120m sale/distribution line is $253m
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unpurged nonrecurring gain increases FY2025 net income and anchor OE, which is then capitalized through the forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The net gain on sales and distribution of other assets in 2025 includes an $89 million gain related to the distribution of certain merchant contracts for the redemption of a minority partner’s membership interest.
audit_findings.explanation: The gains are demonstrated, but their inclusion in the $4,490.8m anchor is not. Even assuming the full $253m upper bound remained in OE and reduced the anchor dollar for dollar, the base buy-below threshold would fall by about $4.57 to approximately $78.85, still materially above the $53 price. The finding therefore does not change the conclusion on the filed scale.
audit_findings.action: Trace the anchor from filed net income and document reversals for the $120m sale/distribution line, $51m equity-method gain and $82m other investment gains, including applicable taxes and overlap; rerun if any amount remains.

audit_findings.title: The anchor tax rate contains discrete benefits
audit_findings.magnitude: $217m of filed 2025 benefits: $55m excess tax benefit from share-based awards, $96m transferable federal tax credits and $66m foreign tax credits
audit_findings.mechanism: Nonrecurring tax benefits raise after-tax anchor OE and are capitalized through the forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The effective income tax rate as a percentage of income before income taxes and income (loss) from investments in unconsolidated affiliates in 2025 included discrete tax benefits from equity compensation and transferable federal and foreign tax credits, resulting in a lower effective income tax rate compared to the statutory income tax rate.
audit_findings.explanation: The benefits are quantified, but the record does not demonstrate that they are nonrecurring or absent from the anchor normalization; transferable-credit benefits also occurred in earlier years. Even removing all $217m from anchor OE would reduce the base buy-below threshold by about $3.92, to approximately $79.50 versus the $53 price. That documented scale cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the anchor's tax provision to the 2025 rate table, distinguish repeatable purchased-credit economics from discrete benefits, and rerun with any nonrecurring $55m, $96m and $66m components removed dollar for dollar.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $117m in FY2018, $765m in FY2022 and $913m in FY2023; computed direct impact on the $4,490.8m FY2025 anchor is $0
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible residual D&A would increase historical OE and could influence growth judgment, but it does not enter the latest-actual anchor under the MIN(trend, latest) rule.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2018 $117.0m (21.0% of filed D&A); FY2022 $765.0m (24.1% of filed D&A); FY2023 $913.0m (29.3% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The treatment is explicitly conservative and cannot overstate value. The supplied residuals relate only to 2018, 2022 and 2023; the valuation anchors to FY2025 because the $6,032m trend exceeds the latest actual. Reclassifying these historical amounts therefore leaves the anchor unchanged, and no filed evidence quantifies an effect on the selected 0%, 3% and 6% growth scenarios.
audit_findings.action: Classify the residual D&A components only if historical growth is reconsidered; rerun the OE history and reassess growth scenarios if filed evidence identifies eligible non-economic amortization, but retain the $4,490.8m anchor absent a supported FY2025 adjustment.
